modelo-professor.d: A stronger model used to generate another model's training data (answers for SFT, candidates for preference pairs). In the post-training recipe, it's Module 1's GLM recipe served on the Sparks. Check that its license allows training another model on its outputs.

llm-as-judge.d: Using a language model to compare or score answers instead of a human. It has known biases (position, verbosity, self-preference, limited reasoning), mitigated with position swapping, an explicit rubric, a judge from another family and a panel of judges.

vies-de-posicao.d: An LLM judge's tendency to prefer the answer in a fixed position (A or B) regardless of its content. Mitigation: judge in both orders and count it as a tie when the verdict flips.

autopreferencia.d: An LLM judge's bias toward giving higher scores to text from its own model family. That's why the judge should come from a family different from both the teacher's and the student's.

descontaminacao.d: Removing from the training set any items that overlap with the evaluation sets (for example, by long normalized n-grams or MinHash). Without it, the benchmark measures memorization instead of capability.

assistant-only-loss.d: An option of TRL's SFTTrainer that computes the loss only on the tokens generated by the assistant, delimited by the template's {% generation %} tags. On Qwen3.8, it swaps the template for qwen3_8_training.jinja.

reasoning-content.d: The assistant message field that holds the reasoning in Qwen3.x templates. The template renders it inside <think>…</think>; putting the reasoning inside content produces two thinking blocks.

dwq.d: mlx-lm's Distilled Weight Quantization: quantizes to few bits by tuning scales and biases through distillation from the unquantized model (the teacher), using calibration data. It works best from 2 to 4 bits.

qlora.d: LoRA trained on top of a base model frozen at 4 bits (NF4 with double quantization in bitsandbytes; 4-bit affine in MLX). It saves memory, but the adapter learns to correct the quantized base, which exacts a price at merge time.

lora.d: Low-Rank Adaptation: freezes the weight \(W_0\) and trains a low-rank update \(s\,BA\), with \(B\) starting at zero. It trains few parameters (\(r(d_{in}+d_{out})\) per matrix) and can be merged into the weight afterwards.

trl.d: Hugging Face's library for post-training (SFT, DPO, KTO, GRPO, reward models, distillation). Stable 1.x since March 2026; PPOTrainer was removed in 1.13.0.

mlx-lm-lora.d: A community package that extends mlx-lm with DPO, ORPO, CPO, GRPO, PPO and other training modes on Apple Silicon. Version 3.1.3 has neither KTO nor SimPO, and it fuses the adapter at the end by default.

gradient-checkpointing.d: A technique that keeps only each layer's input during the forward pass and recomputes the rest during the backward pass. It trades activation memory for an extra forward (from ~4N to ~6N FLOPs per token in a LoRA run).

caminho-rapido-gdn.d: The flash-linear-attention (fla) and causal-conv1d kernels that transformers uses for Gated DeltaNet. Without them, the code falls back to a pure-PyTorch path that is silent and several times slower.

ddp.d: Distributed Data Parallel: each process holds the whole model, processes a slice of the data, and only the gradients cross the network (all-reduce). Ideal when the model fits on each node.

fsdp.d: Fully Sharded Data Parallel: shards weights, gradients and optimizer state across processes (like ZeRO-3) and gathers the weights with an all-gather at every forward and backward. It saves memory at the cost of much more communication.

kto.d: An alignment method that uses binary labels (desirable or undesirable response) instead of pairs. In TRL, the KL term is estimated by pairing each prompt with a completion from another example in the batch, so it requires a per-device batch larger than 1.

frac-reward-zero-std.d: A GRPO metric in TRL: the fraction of groups in which every completion got the same reward. In those groups the advantage is zero and there's no signal; a value near 1 means the dataset is too easy or too hard for the model.

vantagem-de-grupo.d: In GRPO, each completion's reward minus its group's mean (G samples from the same prompt), divided by the standard deviation. It replaces PPO's critic with a baseline estimated among siblings.

likelihood-displacement.d: A DPO phenomenon in which the log-probability of the chosen response falls during training while the margin rises, because the rejected one falls faster. Probability mass can migrate to responses with the opposite meaning; anchoring the chosen response with NLL, raising β or filtering out very similar pairs (CHES score) mitigates the problem.

recompensa-implicita.d: In DPO, \(\hat r_\theta(x,y)=\beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y|x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y|x)}\): the reward the trained model defines relative to the reference. It's what TRL logs under rewards/*.

win-rate.d: The fraction of pairwise comparisons the candidate wins against a baseline, with a tie worth half a point: \((W+T/2)/n\). Report it with a confidence interval (per-prompt bootstrap).

wr-lc.d: Win rate adjusted by a logistic regression with the length difference between the answers as a covariate; the reported value is the prediction with the difference set to zero. It neutralizes part of the judges' verbosity bias.

portao-de-decisao.d: A pass criterion written down before seeing the results (for example, the lower bound of the WR-LC CI above 50%). Preregistering keeps you from picking the checkpoint that happened to do best on the last benchmark you looked at.

merge-de-adaptador.d: Adding the LoRA product to the weight, \(W' = W_0 + s\,BA\), and saving the resulting model. After the merge, inference pays nothing for the adapter; do it on the BF16 base, not on the 4-bit one.

llm-compressor.d: The vLLM project's library for quantizing checkpoints into the compressed-tensors format (W4A16, FP8, NVFP4…), with GPTQ, AWQ and its own calibration. It has official recipes for Qwen3.8-27B.

modelopt.d: NVIDIA Model Optimizer: NVIDIA's quantization tool (FP8, NVFP4) with per-model recipes, such as the local Hessian one used for nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4. The example paths changed between versions: pin the version.

kl-de-deriva.d: Per-token KL(base‖fine-tuned), teacher-forced: it measures how much post-training changed the model. It should be large on the trained domain and small on generic text; don't confuse it with the quantization KLD.

model-diff.d: An exllamav3 script (eval/model_diff.py) that compares two models with real weights and kernels: perplexities, KL in both directions, top-K and KL by confidence band. In it, model B (-mb) is the reference.

piso-de-ruido.d: The value of a metric measured between two runs of the same model (another boot, another batch). An effect smaller than this floor doesn't exist; the GLM recipe uses the "stock vs stock" floor in its KLD panel.

max-loras.d: A vLLM flag: how many distinct LoRA adapters can be active in the same batch, that is, how many slices the stacked \(A\) and \(B\) buffers have on the GPU. Default 1; a request whose adapter has no free slice waits.

max-lora-rank.d: A vLLM flag that sets the width \(r_{\max}\) of every slice of the LoRA buffers (default 16; accepts 1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 320 and 512). A lower-rank adapter only fills part of the slice, and the leftover zeros still cost memory and compute in shrink and expand: use the largest actual rank.

shrink-expand.d: The two batched kernels that apply LoRA per token in a mixed batch: shrink computes \(v_t = A_{\sigma(t)}x_t\) (from \(d_{in}\) to \(r_{\max}\)) and expand adds \(s\,B_{\sigma(t)}v_t\) to the base output, fetching the matrices from the slice of each token's slot \(\sigma(t)\). Descendants of Punica's SGMV/BGMV.
